AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Stroke is a disastrous disease and a major health burden worldwide, especially in Korea. Hemorrhagic stroke (HS) accounts for approximately 20% of all the types of strokes. It is important to be able to evaluate stroke diagnoses and evolving treatments.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: We aimed to identify the top-100 cited articles and assess a paradigm shift that occurred in the field of HS.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: We searched all articles that had been cited more than 100 times using the Web of Science citation search tool during January 2016. Among a total of 2,651 articles, we identified the top-100 cited articles on HS.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The number of citations for the articles analyzed in this study ranged from 1,746 to 211, and the number of annual citations ranged from 125.6 to 5.5. Most of the articles that were published in Stroke (35%) and Journal of Neurosurgery (22%), originated in the United States (n = 56), were original articles (64%), and dealt with the natural history or etiology (n = 37) and vasospasm in subarachnoid hemorrhage (n = 8).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: We analyzed the top-100 cited articles in the field of HS based on citation rates. The results provide a unique perspective on historical and academic developments in this field.
